description: Canada's first National Infrastructure Assessment, released on 27 November 2025 as Building Foundations for Tomorrow: Assessing Housing-Enabling Infrastructure Across Canada, examines water and wastewater, public transit and active transportation, and solid waste systems and the pressure that population growth and climate change put on them. The Canadian Infrastructure Council, an arm's-length expert advisory body set up by the Minister of Housing and Infrastructure in December 2024, produced it after engagement across Canada in 2025, a What We Heard report and technical papers on clean water and sanitation, solid waste and transit. The minister has asked the Council for a second report with the same housing focus. Coverage is Canada. Format and access: reports and technical papers on the Council's website, linked from the government page. Licence: Government of Canada terms, not read; free. Caveats: the report itself was not opened here, only the government summary page, and its scope is limited to housing-enabling systems. It provides planning context and capacity gaps for capacity planning and climate adaptation models of Canadian municipal infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the OECD review of national risk assessments and the CDRI Global Infrastructure Resilience Report 2025.
